newsitem.title: FRANCE: France plans "smart bracelet" as jail substitute.
newsitem.headline: France plans "smart bracelet" as jail substitute.

text.p: French deputies approved on Tuesday a plan to authorise surveillance of offenders with short sentences through electronic "smart bracelets" as a substitute for jail.
The plan, already approved by the Senate, was endorsed at a first reading by members of the centre-right ruling coalition, with Socialists and Communists abstaining.

The text provides for a judge to decide on his own initiative, or at the prompting of the prosecutor or the offender himself, to order the measure for anyone sentenced to jail terms totalling no more than a year, or with a year at most left to purge.
The scheme aims to prevent offenders sentenced to brief jail terms from coming into contact with more heavily-punished counterparts.
Participants in the scheme would wear a bracelet around the wrist or ankle and would be forbidden from moving more than 45 metres (150 feet) away from a transmitter set up in their home.
